not_covered.text: Itineraries with an international leg: the on-time data covers US domestic flights only.
Itineraries with two or more connections.
Connections between flights bought as separate tickets, which are not sold routings in DB1B.
Flights of airlines that do not report on-time data to BTS, including most regional partners flying under their own code.
Routes, hubs and itineraries not listed here: the showcase is a curated selection, not every connection through the hubs.

definitions.text: The scheduled layover that would have left enough time on the configured share of operated days, rounded up to 5 minutes, shown with the itinerary's median scheduled layover and the share of operated days on which its scheduled layover was at least that long.
Difference in connection feasibility between two comparable itineraries on the same route, in points, with a paired bootstrap interval over the days both were flown.
Share of eligible days on which the two scheduled flights connected within the layover limits.
Another outbound flight from the hub that the same inbound flight connected to, with its own feasibility.

Share of the paired days in the data period on which the inbound flight's actual arrival left at least the minimum connection time plus the boarding cutoff before the outbound flight's actual departure, with both flights operated. A historical frequency for the data period, not a prediction.
A labelled, sourced event in the data period shown beside the monthly view; never used in any calculation.
Days on which the connection was not feasible, by reason: too little time between operated flights, a cancelled leg, or a diverted leg.
A comparable itinerary on the same route with a shorter travel time whose feasibility, by the paired interval, was no more than the configured margin lower.
Fewer paired days than the minimum sample; no rate is shown, only the count.
Scheduled minutes between the inbound arrival and the outbound departure at the hub, the median over connecting days.
Connection feasibility within one calendar month; months below the monthly minimum sample show the count only.
Travel time divided by the typical scheduled nonstop time between the same airports, when a nonstop was flown in the data period.

Days in the data period on which the itinerary's two flights were scheduled to connect and passed the data-quality checks, including days a leg was cancelled or diverted (counted as not feasible); the sample behind each rate.
A lasting change in a leg's scheduled departure time within the data period.
Of the minimum-connection-time and boarding-cutoff settings tested, how many kept both itineraries comparable with the same order.

Minutes between the inbound flight's actual arrival and the outbound flight's actual departure on one paired day. The connection was feasible that day when the slack was at least the transfer time (minimum connection time) plus the boarding cutoff and neither leg was cancelled or diverted.
Sampled DB1B passengers on this routing (both airlines, through this hub) in the data period, shared by the itineraries on the routing.

The scheduled layover is shorter than the minimum connection time plus the boarding cutoff at the median, or on more than 10% of connecting days; on those days the connection was feasible only when the inbound was early or the outbound late.
Scheduled minutes from departure at the origin to arrival at the destination, the median over connecting days.
